entries.en: I got the transponder frequency for his new ship, but I just can't get anyone to check it out.
I was hoping you'd say that. But, Commander, take me with you when you go. If it is Saleon, I want to be there when you find him.
Thanks for hearing me out. I appreciate it.
Are you worried that the Council might be protecting Saren?
We'll catch him. Just be ready when we do.
I need to go. So long, Garrus.
I gotta go.
You've seen this before on the Citadel?
Do you have any idea what happened to Dr. Saleon?
I'll check out the coordinates when I get a chance.
Is this common?
Dr. Saleon
Commander. I hear you dealt with Dr. Saleon.
I wish you'd taken me with you.
So I heard. It's just... I've been waiting to nail him for years.
I'm a bit upset, yeah. I've been hoping to nail him for some time.
Well, at least he's dead.
You'll be glad to know he's dead.
You mad that I took your kill?
You upset?
It's hard to let go of something like that.
I... All right.
You'll get over it.
You worry too much, Garrus. We'll catch him soon enough.
I've gotta go.
Quit whining.
No. Goodbye.
So, this is what working with a Spectre is like.
I suppose I will.
I suppose it is.
You think you've got us Spectres figured out?
The mission comes first, Garrus. I wanted someone else at my back for this one.
Sometimes things don't work out the way we'd like. That's just life, Garrus.
You haven't seen a thing.
No doubt.
I didn't need you.
Quit worrying.
You were right about Dr. Saleon, too. Killing him was the only solution.
And I think I understand why you acted the way did with Saleon. Hesitating is the worst thing in a situation like that.
I can see that now.
And I've been thinking about Dr. Saleon too. I'd convinced myself that he deserved to die, but then I started thinking about why I wanted him dead.
Saren is going to pay with his life! I'll make sure of it.
We'll bring Saren to justice. He can't evade us forever.
I hope we find that bastard Saren soon.
We've got to stop Saren before he can hurt anyone else.
I like the way you do things around here, Commander.
Commander. I'm beginning to see why they made you a Spectre.
That's quite a speech, Garrus.
See you later, Garrus.
That's great, Garrus.
Thanks. I think.
You bet.
There's more to it than that.
C-Sec's handling of Saren was typical. I just couldn't take it anymore. I hate leaving....
Yeah. You're probably right.
Yeah. I suppose you're right.
Well, that's sort of why I teamed up with you. It's a chance for me to get off the Citadel, see how things are done outside C-Sec.
Either way, I plan to make the most of this.
Commander. How are you?
Hm. That's a good question. There were several reasons, I guess.
Probably the same as most officers. I wanted to fight injustice, wanted to help people.
I guess my father had something to do with it, too. He was C-Sec. One of the best.
I grew up hearing about his accomplishments or seeing his picture on the vids after a big arrest.
He's taking my resignation pretty hard.
My father's a C-Sec man to the bone. "Do things right, or don't do them at all," he says.
He thinks I'm being too rash. Too impatient. He's worried I'll become just like Saren.
He actually talked me out of becoming a Spectre when I was younger. For the same reasons.
Well, I was targeted as a possible Spectre candidate. Me and about a thousand other turian military recruits.
I could have received special training, but my father didn't like it.
So you just quit because you didn't like the way they do things?
You did the right thing. Life's too short to sit around waiting for things to happen.
It's not the end of the world. You'll have tougher decisions soon enough.
I hope you made the right choice. I'd hate for you to regret it later.
Why did you want to be a C-Sec Officer in the first place?
He's not impressed that you're going after Saren?
That's tough. But you'd think he'd be impressed you're going after Saren.
You were asked to be a Spectre?
That was your reason?
It's a tough decision.
You and C-Sec.
I can understand that.
A Spectre?
Yeah. It's a speech I've heard one too many times.
You can?
But Saren's not going to play by our rules. C-Sec's rules.
If you want to nail Saren, you need to send someone who isn't restricted by policies and procedures.
I see what you mean, but... I'll think about it.
I'm right behind you, Commander.
Good point.
I'm going to reapply for Spectre training. It will probably kill my father, but I've got to try.
If that doesn't work, I'll do just about anything... except go back to C-Sec. I'm done with them.
No more red tape. No more politics. From now on, I do things my way.
Well, I'm going to go back to C-Sec. I think I can make a difference there.
I'll also reapply for Spectre training. But I'll do it right. I won't compromise myself to get there.
Just because you can break the rules, doesn't mean you should. I don't need to stoop to Saren's level to stop him. And neither do you, Garrus.
You're a quick learner, Garrus. We'll beat him at his own game. It's the only way to stop someone like him.
Don't get caught up in the details, Garrus. We'll find him and then we'll stop him. That's all you need to know.
Not true.
Don't tell me that!
Don't let me down.
Looking for supplies?
Whatever you want. Armor, weapons, mods... it's not standard Alliance issue, but that's not necessarily a bad thing.
Well, as long as you don't mind paying for it.
My stuff doesn't come from the Alliance. I have to purchase it myself, and it's not cheap.
Hell, the licenses alone have set me back more than I'd like. But, no licenses, no goods. Without the goods, I'm out of a job.
No problem. Keep checking back.
Manufacturers sell licenses. Each license allows me to buy and sell a certain brand of products.
I already have several basic ones, but you'll need to buy more if you want me to bring in different brands.
Many of the best licenses are hard to get, but they're well worth the cost if you can find them.
Well, that depends on how many licenses you've purchased, but I'll rotate items on a regular basis, regardless.
And any time we land someplace with a big enough port, I'll buy, sell, and trade whatever I can.
Check back often. I need to move items quickly, so only the most basic items will be stocked consistently.
Hey, Commander. Looking for some extra supplies before you head out?
What have you got?
Why should I pay you for my weapons and armor?
Not right now, thanks.
Let's see what you've got.
What are licenses? Why do you need them?
How often will you get new items?
Supplies?
Pay you?
Maybe later.
Show me.
Licenses
New items
There are too many for me to keep track of, but each license will explain what it's good for.
What do the different manufacturers offer?
Manufacturers?
It was an honor working with you, Commander Shepard. Despite the losses, our mission was a success.
Lieutenant Alenko's actions will not go unnoticed. His sacrifice has earned humanity a great deal of respect from my people.
My superiors will duly honor Chief Williams for her actions. Her sacrifice has earned humanity a great deal of respect from my people.
The loss of a trusted ally is never easy to accept. It is a shame that the greatest among us are prone to such sacrifices.
Indeed. I understand the two of you had a personal connection. "First circle" losses are always the hardest to bear.
Of course. A grim reality that every soldier must accept.
Rest assured, Commander, my men and I will not forget what you have accomplished here.
It is remarkable we managed to escape with as many people as we did. It speaks to the quality of your leadership and your officers.
My superiors will hear of this. You have made an ally of the salarian people.
I salute you and all of your officers.
My men were concerned about teaming with you, but your actions have earned their respect.
We will work together again; I am certain of it.
A good officer's worth a lot more than your respect. I'd rather have him back.
He knew what the risks were.
A good soldier's worth a lot more than your respect. I'd rather have her back.
She knew what the risks were. Any of my officers would have done the same.
I don't want your respect.
We all face tough choices.
We will leave your ship as soon as you reach your next destination. Perhaps we will have the opportunity to work together again some day.
Under exceptional circumstances, we are each called upon to do exceptional things.
I get the job done. No matter what.
We did what we had to.
